target: Round-19 route "hk-law-certificate": a necessary condition for one-player realisability of a cube orientation beyond Holt-Klee (hkc:facet, hkc:obstruction, hkc:realised, hkc:main), claiming s_0 = (8,9,10,11,13,12,14,15,7,6,4,5,3,2,1,0) is Holt-Klee but not one-player realisable.
verdict:
SOUND. I reconstructed every step of hkc:facet and hkc:obstruction by hand from the definitions and rebuilt every computational claim independently in exact rational arithmetic; nothing fatal or major survives. Only five notes and one minor write-up slip.

WHAT I RE-DERIVED BY HAND (proof audit).
(1) b_v(sigma)=1 iff D_v(x_sigma)>0, with D_v=Psi_{v,1}-Psi_{v,0} affine and of zero coefficient at x_v: correct from def:readout-system and lem:readout-reduce.
(2) hkc:facet. Freezing u at a gives (def:subcube, lem:subgame(a),(b)) a stopping one-player game whose value vectors are x_sigma restricted and whose improvement outmap is s|_H; D_u is an affine functional of exactly the free values and is nonzero with the sign of b_u by nondegeneracy. Sound. (One write-up slip, finding #1.) Remark (f)'s extension to a 3-subcube with a frozen coordinate also holds: on a subcube the frozen block's values are an affine function of the free ones, (I-P_FF) being invertible by stopping, so D_u is still affine in the free values.
(3) hkc:obstruction. Every algebraic step checks: b(sigma)=4 for sigma<=3 and 7 for sigma>=4, hence sign D_0 = sign D_1 = 2 sigma_2-1 and delta_sigma>0; the four order relations of eq-order are exactly four single improving switches, strict at the switched coordinate by lem:switch (whose text I read: "with strict inequality at every v in S"). The shear formula D(i,j,k,l)=delta_k[u_iu_ju_l]-delta_l[u_iu_ju_k] is right INCLUDING its global sign (the "1"-column sits last, contributing (-1)^{1+4}); the degenerate case D(i,j,k,l)=-delta_l[u_iu_ju_k] is right. eq-VL/eq-VM verified case-by-case on sigma_0 = a, > a, < a. The gradients g_{a,c}, h_{b,c} and the positivity of their first/second components (a product p^{0,a}_2 p^{2,c}_0 = 1 forces q=0 and all other entries 0, i.e. a two-cycle trap against lem:trapchar) are right. The line identities follow from det(g^perp,z) = -g.z with rows, and the four scalars B,A,B',A' pick out exactly the right (a,c)/(b,c) pairs. The five determinant evaluations, the triangle identity [acw]=[abw]+[bcw]-[abc], both expressions E1 and E2, and the complementary-branch disjunction on delta_5 vs delta_6 all check. The Radon coefficients mu_i = (-1)^{pos} det(rest) satisfy sum mu_i Y_i = 0 (Cramer), and their signs (-,+,-,-,+) on (0,2,3,5,6) match chi. Sound.
(4) hkc:main. b(s_0) = (8,8,8,8,9,9,8,8,15,15,14,14,15,15,15,15) recomputed by hand; the facet at (u,a)=(0,0) read on coordinates 1,2,3 is exactly t=(4,5,6,7,3,2,1,0), and b_0 there is exactly chi with chi^{-1}(1)={2,4,6,7}. Sound.

WHAT I REBUILT COMPUTATIONALLY (all exact, my own code, from the statements).
- Cube tools validated: 3-cube 744 USOs, 728 acyclic, 18 AUSO classes, 16 Holt-Klee (matches prop:m3-realised). 4-cube enumerated from scratch: 5541744 USOs, 4792176 acyclic, 12640 classes; my orbit set EQUALS the census used by round 18; heights 1,754,4776,5404,1561,143,1 and 6113 Holt-Klee reproduced, my Holt-Klee max-flow test agreeing with the census flag on all 12640.
- t: AUSO, sink 7, walk 0,4,7 (height 2), Holt-Klee. s_0: AUSO, sink 15, walk 0,8,15 (height 2), Holt-Klee, class index 2490.
- All 43 distinct readout systems reloaded and re-analysed: substochastic, zero self-entry, outmap t, nondegenerate; 7 with delta_5>delta_6 and 26 with delta_5=delta_6; the five determinants have the claimed signs; the Radon mu has the signs of chi with sum mu = 0 and sum mu y = 0; the chi-separation LP is infeasible on all 43. I then recomputed EVERY closed form of the proof (eq-d1, eq-d2, eq-d3, E1, E2, K = -A'D_1(y_3), positivity of A,A',B,B',K) as exact equalities on all 43: 0 failures.
- FROM THE GAME: T3_game0.json (N=37) rebuilt with my own trap test (lem:trapchar, over non-sinks) and my own exact linear solver: greatest trap empty, one player, outmap t, least gap 522241/1048576, the printed eight value vectors and the printed mu = (-534252543/2147483648, 534252543/1073741824, -534252543/2147483648, -1023/4096, 1023/4096) reproduce exactly. T3_big_game0.json likewise (trap empty, outmap t, mingap 34358951937/68719476736, signs and mu correct).
- FROM THE GAME, 4 Max: M4_game0.json (N=138, 4 Max, 132 avg, 2 sinks): trap empty, outmap equals the published class outmap, mingap 1485575/67108864 as claimed. I then computed Psi_{u,a}(x_{sigma,-u}) from the game by retyping the other Max vertices as terminals of payoff x_sigma and solving exactly: Psi_{u,sigma_u} = x_sigma(u) at all 64 (u,sigma), D_u is nonzero with the sign of b_u at all 64, and all 8 facet data are separable. This is a direct game-level confirmation of hkc:facet.
- THE EXCLUSION SCAN, reimplemented from the definition: exactly 17 of the 12640 classes carry a facet datum in the 96-element orbit of (t,chi); 13 are Holt-Klee, of heights 2,3,4 with multiplicities 3,6,4; my 13 representatives coincide with the list printed in hkc:main, and the witnesses (u,a) coincide with excluded_17.json. The other 4 are non-Holt-Klee, so already excluded by prop:oneplayer-lp.
- THE FALSIFICATION TEST: all 13 excluded Holt-Klee classes lie in round 18's unsolved162; NONE of round 18's 5951 realised classes is excluded. Stronger: I took 400 of round 18's exact realised systems, recomputed their configurations exactly (all 400 outmaps equal their class representative), and ran the separation test on all 3200 facet data - all separable, with the separating functional confirmed in exact arithmetic. Any failure here would have refuted the law.
- STRICTNESS OVER cor:b2-min: I reimplemented the forbidden-pair test from cor:b2-min's own statement (g_i = b_i, confirmed from prop:rows-turn's definition) and reproduced its published counts exactly - 0 of the 6113 Holt-Klee classes, 4365 of the 6527 others - and s_0 has no forbidden pair. The new law is therefore genuinely stronger and is not that test in disguise.
- Random sampling: 60000 random substochastic affine 3-state systems produced 27 realising t, all with the predicted determinant sign vector.

STANDING-ERROR SWEEP: no greedy policy iteration anywhere (one-player val_sigma by exact linear solve); the trap is taken over non-sinks per lem:trapchar; my rebuilds accumulate row coefficients rather than using dict literals; the sinks are carried as sentinels n, n+1; the route makes no stall, barrier, algorithm, oracle or polynomial-class claim, so the standing decision-rule and the target-equivalences (thm:decide-one-bit, thm:top, thm:gap-equivalence, ...) are not engaged; no fifth theorem is imported (the certificate is exhibited, not invoked; Holt-Klee is one of the four allowed, and its max-flow test uses Menger as elsewhere in the paper).

MY OWN SEARCH WAS INCONCLUSIVE AND IS NOT EVIDENCE: an independent CEM optimiser over the 8 rows failed even on a control class known to be realisable (best min-margin -8.8e-8 on class 205), so it can neither corroborate nor contradict the route's "-7.3e-5 .. -1.1e-4" figures. Those figures are search evidence, and the route correctly does not present them as a result; they should not enter the paper as evidence either.

The headline is a sentence the route proved, in the words of hkc:main.

findings.defect: The proof asserts that freezing u at a gives "a stopping game with m-1 Max vertices by lem:subgame(a)". lem:subgame/def:subcube do NOT deliver that: G_C keeps u as a Max vertex with both out-edges redirected to the same target, so G_C formally has m Max vertices and, worse, the incidence (sigma,u) is TIED in G_C, i.e. G_C is degenerate at u - exactly the hypothesis co-realisability requires (a NONDEGENERATE one-player game with m-1 Max vertices). The step is asserted, not proved.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex def:subcube ("The subgame G_C is G with BOTH out-edges of each v in F redirected to rho(v)") and lem:subgame(a) ("Formally G_C still has 2^{|Vmax|} Max strategies, but the choices at the fixed vertices are inert because both their out-edges coincide"). MISSING SENTENCE, and it repairs the step: retype u in G_C as an average vertex whose two successors are both u^{(a)}; the resulting game is one-player with exactly m-1 Max vertices, nondegenerate, has the same value vectors, and is stopping because any trap U of it is a trap of G (at u both successors lie in U, so some successor does, which is the controlled-vertex condition of lem:trapchar). Everything downstream is unaffected; I verified the conclusion of hkc:facet directly from a built 4-Max game (M4_game0.json, N=138): Psi_{u,sigma_u}(x_{sigma,-u}) = x_sigma(u) and sign D_u(x_sigma) = b_u(sigma) at all 64 pairs (u,sigma), and all 8 facet data separable.

findings.defect: Step 5 says "every term mu_i phi(y_i), i in S, would be strictly positive". Under hkc:def-datum, which only requires phi(y_sigma) > 0 EXACTLY WHEN chi(sigma)=1 (so phi may vanish where chi = 0), the three terms with chi = 0 are only >= 0. The stated reason is false as written.
findings.evidence: The contradiction nevertheless stands, because mu_2 phi(y_2) > 0 and mu_6 phi(y_6) > 0 are strict while the other three terms are >= 0, so the sum is > 0, not 0. Fix by writing "every term is >= 0 and the terms at i = 2, 6 are > 0". In the application (hkc:facet) phi = D_u is nonzero everywhere by nondegeneracy, so nothing is lost.

findings.defect: The isomorphism of facet data allows carrying chi to its COMPLEMENT, but co-realisability as defined is strict only on the chi = 1 side and is therefore not literally invariant under complementation; the 17-class scan uses complemented data (the orbit has 96 elements, 48 automorphisms times complement).
findings.evidence: I checked that for THIS datum the Radon argument covers the complement as well: with phi > 0 exactly on chi^{-1}(0) one gets mu_0 phi(y_0), mu_3 phi(y_3), mu_5 phi(y_5) < 0 and mu_2 phi(y_2), mu_6 phi(y_6) <= 0, so the sum is < 0, again contradicting 0. The scan's count of 17 therefore stands (I reproduced it independently: 17 classes, 13 Holt-Klee of heights 2,3,4 with multiplicities 3,6,4, representatives identical to the printed list). The definition should nonetheless be stated with strict signs on both sides, which is what hkc:facet actually delivers.

findings.defect: "Laplace expansion gives sum_i mu_i Y_i = 0" is asserted without proof.
findings.evidence: It is the standard alternating-minor dependence of five vectors in R^4 (each coordinate of the sum is a 5x5 determinant with a repeated row), one line of linear algebra, and I confirmed it exactly on all 43 systems and on the 37-vertex game (sum mu = 0 and sum mu_i y_i = 0 componentwise). Worth one sentence so that no fifth theorem appears to be imported.

findings.defect: The games_built field states "T3_big_game0.json (N = 61)"; the file actually contains N = 78 (61 is the vertex count of a different entry of T3_big_games_report.json). Also, of the 43 + 3 games claimed to have been built and checked from the game, only three game files are saved (T3_game0.json N=37, T3_big_game0.json N=78, M4_game0.json N=138); the remaining 40 + 2 are attested only by the two report files and the build scripts.
findings.evidence: I verified all three saved game files from the game with my own trap test and exact solver (values, outmaps, least gaps, five determinant signs and the Radon coefficients all reproduce), and I verified all 43 readout systems exactly, so the substance is backed; the vertex count 61 and the completeness of the archived games are reporting inaccuracies only.

findings.defect: The README's "consistency with search" numbers (best min-margin -7.3e-5 .. -1.1e-4 on each of the 13 excluded classes; -2.4e-5 for s_0 over 72 restarts) are search evidence and cannot be corroborated by an independent auditor at this budget.
findings.evidence: My own CEM optimiser over the eight rows reached only -8.8e-8 on class 205, a class round 18 REALISED exactly at denominator 1024 - i.e. my search fails on a positive control, so it discriminates nothing. The route does not present these numbers as a result, and they should not be carried into the paper as evidence; the theorem does not need them.
